title: CKD staging and progression

steps.tx: **KDIGO** defines chronic kidney disease as abnormalities of kidney structure or function persisting for > 3 months, classified into GFR categories G1 (>= 90 mL/min/1.73m2), G2 (60 to 89), G3a (45 to 59), G3b (30 to 44), G4 (15 to 29), and G5 (< 15 or dialysis), reflecting staging.

steps.tx: The **KDIGO heat map** integrates GFR stages (G1 to G5) with albuminuria stages (A1 < 30 mg/g, A2 30 to 300 mg/g, A3 > 300 mg/g) to stratify risks of CKD progression, cardiovascular mortality, and acute kidney injury. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: The 4-variable **Kidney Failure Risk Equation** (KFRE) calculates the 2-year and 5-year risk of developing end-stage kidney disease using age, sex, eGFR, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR). This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: Brenner's **hyperfiltration hypothesis** posits that initial nephron loss induces compensatory hemodynamic adaptation with afferent arteriolar vasodilation and single-nephron GFR elevation, which drives progressive glomerulosclerosis independent of original etiology. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Dietary sodium restriction** to < 2.0 g/day (< 5 g sodium chloride per day) lowers systolic blood pressure, potentiates the antiproteinuric efficacy of RAAS inhibitors, and slows CKD progression. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Metformin** therapy must be dose-reduced to maximum 1,000 mg/day when eGFR is 30 to 44 mL/min/1.73m2 and must be completely discontinued when eGFR falls below 30 mL/min/1.73m2 to prevent lactic acidosis. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice with diagnostic threshold 1000.

steps.tx: Guideline-directed oral **sodium bicarbonate** supplementation targeting serum bicarbonate levels between 22 and 26 mmol/L slows the rate of eGFR decline and improves muscle mass in metabolic acidosis of CKD. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice, reflecting CKD progression.

steps.tx: Referral to specialized nephrology **multidisciplinary care** is strongly recommended when eGFR falls below 30 mL/min/1.73m2 (Stage 4 CKD) or when the 2-year predicted risk of kidney failure by KFRE exceeds 10% to 20%. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.
